transcription.original_script:
№ 4
Попово
Состоялось въ Посадѣ Сероцкѣ Десятаго (Двадцать втораго Ян-
варя, тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года въ одиннадцать
часовъ утра. — Явился лично Моисеева Закона Ицекъ Файбишъ Б
нгеръ, торговщикъ, Двадцати шести лѣтъ отъ роду, въ Деревнѣ
Поповѣ жительствующій, въ присутствіи свидѣтелей Моисеева
Закона Файбеша Розенберга сапожника, сорока лѣтъ отъ
роду и Мортка Фишмана мясника, сорока четырехъ лѣтъ
отъ роду, здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ жительствующихъ, и предъявилъ
намъ младенца женскаго пола, объявляя, что она роди-
лась въ Деревнѣ Поповѣ восьмаго (Двадцатаго) Мая тысяча
восемьсотъ семьдесятъ втораго года въ пять часовъ утра
отъ законной его жены Фрейделяхъ, урожденной Меер-
новой тридцати лѣтъ отъ роду. — Младенцу этому
дано Имя Голда. — Актъ сей по нерадѣнію родителей
опоздано и объявленъ сего дня, объявляющему и свидѣте-
лямъ прочитанъ, и затѣмъ объявляющимъ, свидѣтелями, а
нами подписанъ. —
Jcek Fajbisz Solarz
Мортка Фишманъ
Содержащій Акты Гражданскаго Состоянія
transcription.translation: No. 4. Popowo. It took place in the Posad of Serock on the tenth (twenty-second) of January, one thousand eight hundred seventy-seven, at eleven o'clock in the morning. There appeared in person Icek Fajbisz B[...]nger, of the Mosaic faith, trader, twenty-six years of age, residing in the village of Popowo, in the presence of the witnesses, of the Mosaic faith, Fajbisz Rozenberg, shoemaker, forty years of age, and Mortka Fiszman, butcher, forty-four years of age, both residing here in Serock, and he presented to us an infant of female sex, declaring that she was born in the village of Popowo on the eighth (twentieth) of May, one thousand eight hundred seventy-two, at five o'clock in the morning, of his lawful wife Frejdela, née Meer[...]nowa, thirty years of age. This infant was given the name Golda. This act was delayed through the negligence of the parents and declared this day; it was read to the declarant and the witnesses and thereupon signed by the declarant, by the witnesses, and by us. Jcek Fajbisz Solarz. Mortka Fiszman. Keeper of the Registers of Civil Status.

notes: CONTRADICTS THE BATCH BRIEF, which pins target.language = "pl". Russian in pre-reform orthography throughout the clerk's text.
One of the two autographs is Latin-script Polish; that does not make the act Polish-language.
Registration in the posad, although both the declarant's residence and the birthplace are the village of Popowo.
The -аго tail is firm; the head reads as a д-loop then е then с, which favours Десятаго over Девятаго.

Cross-check with the paired day-word: the Gregorian side reads Двадцать втораго, i.e. 22, and 22 minus 12 is 10, which supports Десятаго. Devjataго would require Двадцать перваго, which is what act 3 actually carries.
Sequence check: act 3 registers on 9 January and act 5 later, so 10 January keeps the register in order.
Month name split across the line 1/2 break; quoted across the break as inked. Gap of 12 days is correct.
Both day-words physically inked.

registration_year.original_script: тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года въ одиннадцать
notes: Excerpt extended past года because the act also carries a second, different year-phrase for the birth.
Split across the line 2/3 break.
The two given names are firm: Ицекъ Файбишъ, read at 8x over source (1180,1280,355,58), and independently confirmed by the Latin autograph Jcek Fajbisz read at 4.8x over source (476,2035,900,62).

The surname is the problem. It begins in the last centimetre of line 3, where the ink runs into the gutter shadow at the page edge, and continues at the start of line 4 as -нгеръ. Only a Б or В-like capital survives from the first part. Crops at 8x over (1180,1280,355,58) and (476,1327,430,58).
The Latin autograph's third token reads as Solarz or Solicwi and does not obviously reconcile with a body form ending -нгеръ, so neither candidate is allowed to overwrite the other.

The same Latin surname shape appears in act 1's signature block beside a different given name (dawid), which may or may not be the same family; that is left as an observation for adjudication rather than resolved here.

Cross-check from act 7 of this register year, whose signature block is the most legible in the group: there the same Latin-script surname shape is unambiguously Solarsz/Solarz. That makes the Soltarz reading given here doubtful, and Solarz is added as a candidate. The Cyrillic body form on this act still does not reconcile with either, so nothing is collapsed.
Standard declarant-is-father construction; also supported by the late-registration clause, which blames родителей, the parents, thereby treating the declarant as one of them.
The word отецъ is not used on this act, unlike act 3.
Read at 8x over source (476,1327,430,58). The tail shows a щ-like descender, which gives торговщикъ, whereas acts 2 and 3 both carry the plainer торговецъ in the same slot.
Retained as a fork because a within-register variant spelling of a recurring word is exactly the case the guidance flags as a misread candidate.

Note the arithmetic tension with the child: a birth in May 1872 would make this declarant about 21 at the time, and the mother 25. Nothing on the act is adjusted to fit; the ages are as stated at registration.

Split across the line 4/5 break. This act gives the clearest instance of the village name in the group: the margin annotation reads Попово at 8x over source (300,1200,190,110), and the body form Поповѣ is unambiguous.
That clarity was used to resolve the same village name on act 1, where the ink is much dimmer.
Same person as the declarant; see declarant.name.

Cross-check from act 7 of this register year, whose signature block is the most legible in the group: there the same Latin-script surname shape is unambiguously Solarsz/Solarz. That makes the Soltarz reading given here doubtful, and Solarz is added as a candidate. The Cyrillic body form on this act still does not reconcile with either, so nothing is collapsed.
Age at registration in 1877, not at the 1872 birth.
Same witness as act 1 of this register year, with the same trade. Read in the genitive.
Note that the declarant's second given name is also Файбишъ; the two are different people and the witness slot is separately introduced by въ присутствіи свидѣтелей.
Agrees with the same man's trade in act 1.
Split across the line 6/7 break. This slot reads as a single decade word without a unit word, which gives 40.

Witness-age continuity: the same man is read as 39 in act 1, registered six days earlier in the same register year. A one-year step across six days is possible if a birthday intervenes, and the guidance treats a step of 0 to 2 years as normal noise rather than a contradiction, but the alternative 39 is retained because it would make the two acts agree exactly.
Plural phrase covering both witnesses.
Third appearance of this witness in the group, after acts 1 and 3, with the same trade and the same stated age each time. Corroborated by the Cyrillic autograph in the signature block.
The surname carries the clerk's underline diacritic under the ш.
Stated as 44 here, in act 1 and in act 3, which is a clean age-continuity result within the register year.

Read at 6.5x over source (476,1844,560,60). The initial has the long horizontal head-stroke this clerk uses for Г, matching his Г in Гаскель on act 3, so a Г initial is preferred and Tojba is the weakest candidate.
Four middle strokes then a final а. Golda fits the stroke count; Goda would need one fewer.
A female name, consistent with the stated female sex.
The only female child among acts 1 to 4. Stated explicitly, and independently corroborated by the feminine что она роди-лась and by the absence of any circumcision wording in the naming slot.
Read at 3.8x over source (476,1615,1054,58).
Gap check: 8 to 20 May is 12 days, correct for the 1870s.
Both day-words inked, with the parenthesis closed.

child.birth_year.original_script: восемьсотъ семьдесятъ втораго года въ пять часовъ утра
notes: Recorded as its own observation because it is the striking fact on this act: the birth year is 1872, five years before registration.

Read at 6x over source (900,1662,640,58). The unit word shows в then an m-form т then орaго, giving втораго. Седьмаго, which would make it 1877, would show a different opening and no m-form in that position.

Corroborated structurally by the late-registration clause on the act, which exists precisely because the act is out of time. An act registered in the year of birth would carry текущаго года instead, as act 3 does.
Agrees with the declarant's residence and with the margin annotation.
Read at 3.8x and 6.5x over source (476,1752,1054,56) and (950,1752,580,56). Фрейде- is firm; the tail is not, and it is not clear whether the clerk wrote one name or ran a double name together.
The terminal -яхъ is unusual for a female given name in this register and is part of why the token is left forked.

Highest-value field and the least well served by this scan. The surname is broken across a line end that also happens to be the page edge, so its middle letters fall into the gutter shadow. Crops made at 6.5x, 7x, 8x and 9x over source (1000,1750,530,58), (1240,1742,295,115), (1050,1752,340,56) and (476,1799,300,56); nothing above about 7x adds information.
What is firm: the née marker урожденной, an initial Меер-, and a terminal -новой at the start of the next line. What is lost: whether anything stands between them.

The -овой ending is a feminine adjectival surname ending rather than the -овны patronymic ending used on act 3, so this is more likely a family surname than a patronymic; the patronymic reading is retained as a third candidate but ranked last.
Deliberately not completed to a familiar surname.
Age at registration in 1877; she would have been about 25 at the stated 1872 birth.

The naming slot runs straight from Младенцу этому to дано Имя Голда with no rite phrase at all. There is no при обрѣзаніи, as this is a girl, but neither is there the при религіозномъ обрядѣ that the formula uses for girls.
BLANK rather than ABSENT_ON_FORM: the formula has the slot and the same clerk fills it on acts 1, 2 and 3 of this register; here he simply omitted it.
Verified by inspecting the junction between the two lines at 6.5x over source (476,1844,560,60) and the preceding line end, to be sure the phrase had not been carried over a line break.

registration_delayed.value: delayed; attributed to the negligence of the parents and declared on the day of registration
registration_delayed.original_script:
Актъ сей по нерадѣнію родителей
опоздано и объявленъ сего дня
notes: The distinguishing feature of this act. Read at 3.8x over source (476,1891,1054,58) and from the band covering the preceding line.
Consistent with the four-and-a-half-year gap between the stated birth of May 1872 and the registration of January 1877, and with the absence of any текущаго года phrasing.
Legitimate birth; the delay is attributed to negligence, not to any irregularity of status.

signatures_note.value: Read to the declarant and witnesses and signed by the declarant, the witnesses and the registrar; one Latin-script and one Cyrillic autograph inked
signatures_note.original_script:
лямъ прочитанъ, и затѣмъ объявляющимъ, свидѣтелями, а
нами подписанъ. —
notes: The clause includes объявляющимъ, so unlike act 3 the declarant did sign, and no illiteracy note appears.

Only two autographs are inked, Jcek Fajbisz Solarz and Мортка Фишманъ, although three signers are named in the formula. Witness 1 Fajbisz Rozenberg, who signed act 1 in Latin script, has no visible autograph here. Recorded as read; not reconciled.

Cross-check from act 7 of this register year, whose signature block is the most legible in the group: there the same Latin-script surname shape is unambiguously Solarsz/Solarz. That makes the Soltarz reading given here doubtful, and Solarz is added as a candidate. The Cyrillic body form on this act still does not reconcile with either, so nothing is collapsed.

officiant.formula.value: Keeper of the Registers of Civil Status
notes: Same subscription and hand as acts 1 to 3.
Zoom inspection performed before emitting ILLEGIBLE: 3.7x over the band covering source (476,1955,1054,208), plus the clearer act 1 instance of the same paraph at 6x over (2350,1090,440,70).
Decorative loops rather than a resolvable name.
Deliberately not filled from the officiant named in the domain skill.

The clearest instance of this village name anywhere in the group; read at 8x over source (300,1200,190,110). Both П letters are unambiguous, which is what settled the п/н question carried over from act 1.
Agrees with the brief's act_no pin.
